2) Streaming requirement: do you require websocket/bi-directional streaming or is chunked SSE (HTTP streaming) sufficient?
3) Network details: would you prefer VPC peering/PrivateLink (recommended) or IPsec VPN? Please share the network contact(s) and an IP range we can validate for peering.
4) We attached our redwood-performance-slo-checklist.pdf and network-test-instructions.txt — please run the tests (or give us a window to run them from our test node).

Hi Sofia / netops team — I'm Aditya (SE, infra). Quick technical notes to help your network team run the tests and set expectations for the POC: 

1) Latency guidance / budgeting: 
- For a typical interactive model (512 tokens), target p95 ~= 120–200ms and p99 ~= 250–400ms depending on model size and quantization. Our recommendation for customer-side network budget: keep TCP RTT <= 30ms where possible; plan ~30–60ms for cross-region peering.
- The overall client-side budget we recommend: 100ms for application + 150–300ms for inference/network combined depending on SLO. If you need sub-200ms p95 at p99 tightness, we'll need peering in the same region and no extra NAT hops.

2) Throughput & concurrency: 
- Your stated baseline (80 sustained RPS, spikes to 250 RPS) is reasonable. For 250 RPS peak, plan for at least 50 concurrent model contexts (depending on request size and batching).
- If you use streaming (websockets), concurrent open connections ~= number of concurrent users; we can multiplex and scale, but please share expected concurrent connections so we can size the pool.

3) Streaming behavior: 
- We support chunked HTTP streaming and websocket-based streaming. Websockets add negligible overhead but require sticky routing for long-lived connections. If you prefer websockets, we'll discuss load-balancer timeouts and keepalives during setup.

4) Networking specifics & tests: 
- Preferred: VPC peering / PrivateLink (lower latency, no internet egress). Backup: IPsec VPN (works but adds jitter and egress).
- NAT/Egress: If your traffic egresses through a NAT gateway, expect an extra 10–40ms and potential burst throttling depending on cloud provider.
- Tests to run (attached instructions): traceroute/mtr from your app subnet to the Redwood test IPs, iperf3 for throughput and jitter, and curl -w "%{time_total}\n" for simple HTTP RTT. Please provide traceroute output and iperf logs.
- Firewall: outbound TLS (443) to Redwood test IPs; we’ll provide a CIDR range. Also allow inbound for peering if we coordinate with your cloud team.

5) Proposed immediate steps: 
- Send us a 1-hour window this week to run active tests from Redwood test node to your test endpoints (we’ll coordinate via netops@acme-corp.com).
- Share expected concurrent connections and any load-balancer timeouts.

I've attached network-test-instructions.txt and included a short checklist in the PDF Marissa sent. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your netops to walk through tests.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
